item.title: Abandoned Bannerman Castle on New York Island Remains a Haunting Historical Site
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: I visited an abandoned castle on a New York island that's only accessible by boat. It was hauntingly beautiful.
Bannerman Castle, built in the early 1900s by Scottish arms trader Francis Bannerman as a fortress, was damaged by a gunpowder explosion in 1920 and abandoned by the 1950s. A fire in 1969 further damaged the structure, leading to its closure by New York state. The Bannerman Castle Trust, in partnership with state parks, restored the site and opened it to the public in 2004. Visitors can tour the island via boat, though access to the castle itself is restricted due to structural risks. The castle’s towers, supported by steel beams, remain unstable, requiring visitors to stay 100 feet away. Parts of the structure collapsed in 2009, and nature has since overtaken much of the site. The island now serves as a museum and historical site, with exhibits detailing its past. The castle’s blend of medieval architecture and overgrown vegetation makes it a unique, hauntingly beautiful landmark accessible only by boat.

item.title: China's families now support more elderly than children
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: China's families are now supporting more old people than kids
China's families now support more elderly people than children, according to official data. The ratio of dependent elderly to working-age population rose to 23% in 2023, surpassing the 22% for children. Over 223 million people aged 65+ now live in China, compared to 213 million children under 14. The shift reflects aging demographics driven by the one-child policy, urbanization, and low birth rates. Experts warn of strain on pensions, healthcare, and long-term care systems, while noting opportunities in the silver economy. Professor Stuart Gietel-Basten called the trend a historical shift, not a short-term phenomenon, and criticized the dependency ratio for overlooking older adults' agency and healthcare improvements. The government has increased financial support for seniors, with over 53 million elderly receiving allowances by 2025. State media highlighted the aging population's economic implications, including potential limits on growth and consumer spending power.

item.title: Mason-Dixon Line Map to Auction for Up to $1.2 Million
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: ‘Dixie’ map that divided US into North and South is going up for auction
A hand-drawn Mason-Dixon Line map, pivotal in dividing free and slave states, is auctioning for up to $1.2 million. Remounted on Japanese rice paper, the document will sell Thursday in a livestreamed auction. Lauren Brunk of Brunk Auctions estimates the anonymous seller could receive between $800,000 and $1.2 million. Originally created to resolve a border dispute between Maryland and Pennsylvania, the line later became central to the Missouri Compromise and the Civil War. Brunk notes the map was not drawn for its later symbolic role. The map, 76 inches long and 6.5 inches tall, was once owned by Benjamin Chew’s family and purchased by Malcolm S. Forbes in 1982 for $360,000, then sold again in 2002. Brunk contacted the Library of Congress, which declined to bid due to budget constraints. The map’s vertical Delaware-Maryland section is at Princeton University.

item.title: Cyclone Arnab kills three in Andhra Pradesh
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: India news: Cyclone Arnab turns deadly after landfall
Cyclone Arnab made prolonged landfall along Andhra Pradesh's coast, killing three people and damaging 31 homes. The storm, downgraded to a severe cyclonic storm, caused widespread flooding, uprooted trees, and disrupted power lines. Authorities evacuated nearly 100,000 residents ahead of the storm. Meanwhile, a Lancet study found India ranks among nations with highest heatwave exposure for infants and the elderly, estimating $174 billion in economic losses from extreme heat in 2025. Jio Platforms, backed by Mukesh Ambani, surged over 21% on its stock market debut, becoming the second-most valuable firm. The UAE honored Indian Captain Smit Machchhar for thwarting a mid-air attack on a Flydubai flight. Cyclone Arnab formed in the Bay of Bengal amid El Nino-driven warming, with officials warning of potential 'total destruction' of vulnerable areas.

item.title: Scientists attempt to restore damaged seagrass meadows in Baltic Sea
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
Conservationists and scientists are working to restore damaged seagrass meadows in the Baltic Sea. Divers carefully transplant shoots from healthy meadows to degraded areas, prioritizing sandy sediment and light conditions. Marine ecologist Thorsten Reusch notes that while 60% of Baltic seagrass has vanished, the decline has halted. Seagrass supports marine life, improves water quality, and stores carbon 30-50 times faster than forests. Projects like ZosteraTec use aquaculture to grow seagrass saplings, which are planted with minimal diving. Researchers also test seed-based restoration, emphasizing genetic diversity. A 2021 planted meadow in the Baltic shows promising growth, with dense shoots and active development. Scientists aim to combine shoot planting with seed sowing to create resilient meadows capable of withstanding climate change.

item.title: U.S. Cruise Ship Halts Global Voyage in Cambodia Over Fuel Costs, Stranding Passengers
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: World, BBC News, San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: U.S. Cruise Ship Suspends Global Voyage in Cambodia Due to Fuel Costs, Stranding Passengers
The MV Odyssey, a U.S. cruise ship operated by Villa Vie Residences, has suspended its three-year around-the-world voyage in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs. Monthly fuel expenses in Asia have surged to $6,000 to $8,000 per cabin, up from an average of $1,800. The company attempted to reduce costs by slowing the itinerary and extending port stays but faced financial strain. The ship, which departed Belfast in October 2024 for a 3.5-year journey, is now docked in Sihanoukville, Cambodia, with no confirmed departure date. Passengers, including 203 residents and 156 crew members, were ordered to disembark after a seven-hour notice. Residents paid between $120,000 and $440,000 for lifetime residencies or $3,500 monthly for cabins. The suspension follows months of financial instability, with passengers reporting repeated fuel cost requests. Some residents, like Paul and Lynn Montoya, cited mismanagement and declining food quality as reasons to leave, while others, such as Carol Larson and Crystal Lavering, expressed devastation. The operator faces restructuring and potential investment challenges, with passengers struggling to find housing in the region. The Odyssey’s suspension marks a setback for the residential cruising concept, which promised global travel and long-term living at sea.
item.source: NPR Topics: World, BBC News, San Diego Union-Tribune

item.title: Mission Bay Sand Berms Remain Stable Amid High Tides
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Mission Bay sand berms hold firm as crews battle one more day of super high tides threatening homes
Sand berms in Mission Bay remain intact despite super high tides, but city officials warn against foot traffic and heavy equipment use. Ben Cartwright, a San Diego City spokesperson, urged residents and visitors to stay off the berms to prevent damage that could lead to breaches during future storms. Crews continue reinforcing the berms, which have been raised since Monday's flooding incident. Homeowner Andrew Kaperonis described his property being flooded for the first time after the berm gave way, showing significant basement damage. City crews are working to strengthen the berms ahead of Wednesday's expected high tides. Parks and Rec confirmed a 6-staff reduction in the beach maintenance team for 2027, though no direct link to Monday's flooding was stated. The berms, built to protect homes from coastal flooding, face ongoing challenges as tides rise.

item.title: Norway and Finland Leaders Hold Direct Call with Putin
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a 90-minute direct call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, marking the first such contact between European leaders and Putin since July 2025. The leaders emphasized the need for direct dialogue on ending Ukraine's war, with Stubb stating the conversation aimed to 'convey messages directly regarding future negotiations.' Both leaders acknowledged 'big differences in views' with Putin, who reiterated Russia's stance on Ukraine's sovereignty and the necessity of 'considering Russia's legal interests.' The call, arranged in consultation with Ukraine and the U.S., preceded planned trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi in November. Zelensky praised the initiative as 'the right approach,' while the EU remained silent. Swedish and Danish leaders urged European unity, noting the talks were not coordinated with other nations. Putin's remarks highlighted Russia's position on the conflict's 'root causes,' and all parties agreed to continue direct communication. The Kremlin described the dialogue as 'constructive,' though European leaders face criticism for engaging with Moscow amid tensions over sanctions and war efforts.

item.title: Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 10,000 Cases, Hits New Milestone
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: World Original headline: The Ebola outbreak is breaking records -- and just marked a grim milestone
The fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in history has surpassed 10,000 infections since its May declaration in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Katie Thomas-Canfield of the International Rescue Committee called the milestone 'staggering,' noting that the current outbreak spans Nigeria to Kenya and has nearly 5,000 deaths, second only to the 2014-2016 outbreak. Children under 5 are disproportionately affected, with three out of four infected dying. WHO regional director Mohamed Janabi emphasized the need for early intervention and trust-building. The outbreak's rapid spread is attributed to delayed detection due to the Bundibugyo strain, which existing tests couldn't detect, plus conflict in the DRC and reduced U.S. foreign aid. International cooperation has been slower than in 2014, when global healthcare workers supported the response. Despite $880 million in pledged funding, resources remain insufficient. Community distrust, fueled by misinformation and rumors, continues to hinder efforts, with 85% of North Kivu residents skeptical of responders. Treatment centers have expanded, but two-thirds of deaths occur outside them. Vaccines for Bundibugyo are not yet available, though trials for existing vaccines are underway. Infectious disease doctor Nahid Bhadelia warned that without sustained funding and trust, the outbreak remains out of control.

item.title: U.S. Stocks Steady as Fed Approaches Rate Decision
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: US stocks hold steady as the countdown ticks to a Federal Reserve decision on interest rates
U.S. stocks edged higher as the Federal Reserve prepares to announce its interest rate decision. The S&P 500 rose 0.2%, nearing its all-time high, while the Dow Jones gained 0.3% and the Nasdaq remained flat. The Fed is expected to leave rates unchanged after a recent hike aimed at curbing inflation, though market focus remains on potential future moves. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has emphasized limiting forward guidance. Tech stocks like Micron Technology and AI firms saw gains, bolstered by SK Hynix’s 10.9% surge following strong earnings. Etsy and GE HealthCare Technologies rose on better-than-expected results. Wendy’s jumped 15.1% after a buyout offer, while Boston Scientific and Robinhood fell due to underperforming reports. Treasury yields climbed to 5.03%, influenced by rising oil prices and Middle East tensions. Global markets also rose, with South Korea’s Kospi up 6.6% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 gaining 1.1%.

item.title: California Coasts Face Record Tides and Flooding
item.description:
Source: Washington Post, LA Times Original headline: Record Tides and Rising Seas Threaten California Coasts
Record high tides caused widespread flooding along California’s coast, submerging areas in Newport Beach, Huntington Beach, and San Diego’s Mission Beach for two days. Tides reached at least eight feet, with San Pedro’s high tide hitting 8.19 feet—the highest since 1923—and Newport Beach recording its highest tide ever at 8.4 feet. The extreme water levels resulted from an intense El Niño event, warm ocean temperatures, and a marine heat wave, with ocean temperatures exceeding normal by over 5 degrees. A full moon amplified tidal forces, while a Kelvin wave from the equatorial Pacific contributed to elevated sea levels. Residents and officials warned of worse flooding in November and December, with Bill Sharp, a Newport Beach resident, calling the situation unprecedented. Local businesses, like Fun Zone Boat Company, faced inundation, and authorities deployed sandbags and pumps to mitigate damage. Officials acknowledged limited effectiveness against the tides, with some roads closed and repairs ongoing after previous storms. The event highlights growing risks from rising seas and climate-driven weather patterns.

item.title: Global Data Center Boom Faces Energy and Community Challenges
item.description:
Source: FP Foreign Policy Original headline: Dawn of the Data Centers
Data centers are expanding globally due to the AI boom, consuming vast amounts of electricity. A United Nations University report states they used more electricity than 10 countries last year, with projections of ranking among the top 5 electricity consumers by 2035. While governments seek economic benefits, communities resist due to environmental and social concerns. The U.S. leads with over 1,500 new data centers, relying on natural gas, while China lags but benefits from cheap land and energy. Emerging markets like India and Indonesia offer cheaper construction costs. Opposition in places like Ireland and India highlights challenges, with legal battles and policy shifts emerging. Analysts note that local pushback will shape the sector’s future, balancing infrastructure needs with community impacts.

item.title: United CEO: Starlink Becomes Key Factor for Airline Choice
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Starlink is fast becoming one of the biggest factors for passengers choosing an airline, United's CEO says
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby says passengers prioritize Starlink over ticket prices when choosing an airline. United, which installed Starlink on nearly half its planes since 2024, noted regional jets have the service but less than 3% of long-haul wide-body jets do. Kirby revealed travelers are opting for regional flights to access Starlink, surprising him. He shared booking a flight to watch a baseball game, saying he’d have booked during the game if Starlink were available. American Airlines has a pending Starlink deal, while Delta uses Amazon Leo, which Musk criticized. Kirby dismissed Musk’s call for Delta CEO Ed Bastian’s firing. United promoted Starlink by matching loyalty status on Delta and American, seeing 275% more sign-ups. Kirby called Starlink 'the biggest competitive advantage' but warned it won’t last as others adopt similar tech.

item.title: Tanzania finds natural gas in Mnazi Bay after decade-long gap
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
Tanzania announced a natural gas discovery in Mnazi Bay, the first in over a decade. The Kasa-1X ST2 well, owned by Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation and Maurel & Prom, holds an estimated 223 billion cubic feet. Energy Minister Juma Homera called it a 'major milestone' for the country's oil and gas sector. Production is set to begin next month, aiming to boost domestic supplies. Tanzania has 57.54 trillion cubic feet of existing reserves. Natural gas provides nearly 80% of the nation's electricity, with compressed natural gas used for vehicles in Dar es Salaam. Some Tanzanians have adopted dual-fuel systems for cheaper costs. The country's first discovery was in 1974 on Songo Songo Island, followed by Mnazi Bay in 1982. Commercialization started in 2004, leading to a 2.7 trillion cubic foot find in 2016.

item.title: Vox Launches Mobile App Integrating Text, Audio, and Video Journalism
item.description:
Source: Vox Original headline: Vox launches mobile app, bringing together text, audio, and video journalism
Vox launched a mobile app integrating text, audio, and video journalism. The free app is available on Apple and Google Play, offering a 14-day trial for non-members. Members access ad-free podcasts and exclusive videos. Editor-in-chief Swati Sharma emphasized the app’s role in uniting Vox’s content across formats, allowing users to explore unfamiliar work. The Home tab features Featured and Latest stories, with a Start Here section for quick summaries. Members enjoy ad-free podcasts like 'Today' and 'America, Actually,' while the Video tab hosts short-form content and in-depth explainers. Vox, founded in 2014, aims to bridge factual reporting with deeper understanding through its multi-platform approach, including YouTube and podcasts. Under Sharma’s leadership, the platform has grown a membership base of tens of thousands.

item.title: Russia's African Strategy: Economic and Military Goals
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
Russia is intensifying its engagement with Africa, focusing on economic partnerships, military influence, and diplomatic leverage. Egypt, the second-largest African economy, is Russia's key partner, with bilateral trade reaching $10.5 billion in 2025, driven by grain and metal exports. Russia is also building a nuclear power plant in Egypt, funded by a $25 billion loan. However, Africa remains a minor trade partner for Russia, accounting for 3.9% of its foreign trade in 2025, far below China's $348 billion and the EU's $385 billion. Military presence includes Wagner Group mercenaries and the Africa Corps in countries like Mali and Libya, with Russia supplying 15% of African arms between 2021–2025. Experts note Russia's diplomatic aim is to bolster its influence in the UN by leveraging Africa's 54 nations. Putin emphasizes collaboration over colonialism, though perceptions vary across the continent. Despite economic limitations, Russia's military and strategic partnerships in Africa aim to secure resources and regional influence.

item.title: Cognition Considers $70B-$80B Funding Round
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: AI coding startup Cognition is weighing a new funding round at a $70 billion to $80 billion valuation
AI coding startup Cognition is considering a new funding round at a valuation between $70 billion and $80 billion, according to sources. The company, founded in 2023 by Scott Wu, Steven Hao, and Walden Yan, previously raised funds at a $48 billion valuation. Current talks involve potential investor interest, though valuation targets remain fluid. Cognition's AI coding agent Devin has attracted major backers including a16z, Accel, and Khosla Ventures. The surge in valuation reflects heightened investor appetite for AI coding tools amid fierce competition. A $75 billion valuation is seen as plausible following SpaceX's $60 billion acquisition of Cursor, another AI coding startup. The company is also embroiled in a public dispute with rival Factory AI, which alleges Cognition employees impersonated job applicants to gather information. Cognition and a former Factory adviser deny seeking or sharing confidential data.

item.title: Ramona Senior Center Lunch Menu: Oct 29–Nov 13
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Ramona senior lunch menu: Oct. 29-Nov. 13
The Ramona Senior Center at 434 Aqua Lane offers in-person dining from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. Monday through Friday. Seniors age 60-plus pay a $5 lunch donation, while non-seniors pay $8. Menu items include teriyaki chicken, brown rice, and tropical fruit on Oct 29; Halloween-themed gouly beef goulash and pineapple on Oct 30; and a Veterans’ lunch featuring chicken cordon bleu and peaches on Nov 10. The center is closed Nov 11 for a holiday. Other days include baked fish, chicken alfredo, spaghetti with ground beef, and beef meat loaf. All meals include milk or fruit. For details, call 760-789-0440.

item.title: California Whale Watchers Encounter Orcas, Great White Shark Near Shore
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Surprising close encounters with marine predators in California bring awe and fear
California whale watchers recorded a rare sighting of 13 Eastern Tropical Pacific orcas off Laguna Beach, with the pod approaching boats within feet. Capt. Matt Stumpf of Capt. Dave’s Whale Watching Safari noted El Niño caused unusually warm waters, extending the orcas’ range northward. The sighting was the third in three weeks for the company. Separately, kayaker David Slavich captured footage of a great white shark approaching his kayak off Half Moon Bay, though the shark did not attack. Marine biologist Chris Lowe explained the shark was following a migration pattern toward northern elephant seal rookeries. State data shows 238 shark-related incidents statewide since 1950, with San Diego leading at 27. Officials emphasized that actual shark encounters are rare compared to reported sightings, with 22 incidents in San Mateo County this decade. Surfing remains the activity most often linked to shark encounters.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Chef Adapts Restaurant Broccoli Dish for Home Cooking
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Crispy broccoli from a restaurant chef gets home makeover
Chef Ayaka Guido of ABC Kitchens in Brooklyn adapted a complex restaurant dish into a home-friendly version. The original crispy broccoli recipe, inspired by Jean-Georges Vongerichten, required specialized tools and multiple steps. Guido simplified it by using roasted broccoli atop garlic-herb white beans and pistachio breadcrumbs with chile. The dish, described as vibrant and vegetarian-friendly, takes about 30 minutes to prepare. Guido noted it’s a 'super-simple thing anyone can make.' The recipe, adapted by Melissa Clark, replaces two vinaigrettes with a protein-rich bean base and layered textures for crunch. It’s served at ABC Kitchens as a standalone dish or alongside proteins. The adaptation balances restaurant-quality flavor with home-cooking ease.

item.title: Dolores Huerta, Labor Rights Leader, Dies at 96
item.description:
Source: ABC News: Top Stories Original headline: Labor rights leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
Labor rights leader Dolores Huerta died at 96, her family announced. Huerta co-founded the United Farm Workers with Cesar Chavez and Gilbert Padilla, leading to the first farmworker union contracts in U.S. history. Her family stated they are grieving the loss and will honor her legacy through future celebrations. Huerta received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012 for her advocacy in civil rights and women’s equality. The family requested privacy during this difficult time, noting global mourning for her impact. The United Farm Workers emerged from the National Farm Workers Association, which she helped establish. Her death marks the end of an era for labor rights movements. The family’s statement emphasized her significance as a mother and activist. Plans to recognize her life and work are in development. This is a developing story with further updates pending.

item.title: Some people with meat allergies from alpha-gal syndrome turn to exotic alternatives
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Health
People with alpha-gal syndrome, a red meat allergy caused by tick bites, are turning to ostrich meat as an alternative. The CDC estimates 450,000 Americans have the condition, which triggers immune reactions to galactose-alpha-1,3-galactose in mammalian meat. Kentucky farmer Brent Williams, diagnosed after a tick bite, began raising ostriches after discovering their meat lacks the allergen. Nutrition professor Abbigail Pace notes ostrich meat is low in fat and contains all essential amino acids. Restaurants like Papaw's Poole Mill, owned by Kenneth Todd, now offer ostrich burgers, drawing customers from afar. Todd plans to expand the menu with ostrich sausage. Mark Geary, another alpha-gal sufferer, praised the meat's flavor, calling it 'fire.' The condition is growing in prevalence as lone star tick populations rise, particularly in the Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, and Deep South.

item.title: San Diego Approves Water Rates Without Conservation Incentives
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: San Diego OKs new water rates that don’t reward conservation to comply with court ruling
San Diego approved new water rates Tuesday that eliminate incentives for conservation, complying with a court ruling that deemed such practices illegal. The decision splits the 14.5% annual increase approved last fall, with larger hikes for low-volume single-family homes and discounts for high-volume users like golf courses and apartments. Low-volume users will pay $5.62 more monthly, while high-volume users see discounts up to $353.52. Councilmembers criticized the court order, calling it a penalty for conservation efforts. The city plans to revisit tiered rates only after 2030, pending analysis and the Supreme Court’s ruling on AB 2180, a state law that could legalize conservation incentives. A subsidy program for low-income residents is under consideration. The rate changes affect 286,000 customers in San Diego and neighboring areas. Protests against the rates totaled 3,644, below the threshold to overturn them.

item.title: Cruise line suspends operations after fuel costs force passenger evacuation
item.description:
Source: Washington Post - World Original headline: Cruise line folds over fuel costs, booting passengers in Cambodia
A residential cruise ship operated by Villa Vie Residences suspended operations in Cambodia after fuel costs surged from $1,800 to over $6,000 per cabin, making it unsustainable to continue. Passengers were abruptly evacuated, with some forced to find their own accommodations. The company stated it had taken steps to reduce fuel use, including altering the itinerary and spending more time in ports, but these measures failed to offset costs. Randy Cassingham, a resident who lived on the ship since late 2024, reported passengers received a 7 a.m. notice to disembark by 2 p.m., with no assistance from the company. Villa Vie said it was working with passengers to find temporary living arrangements but did not disclose the number of affected individuals. The cruise, which sold residences and short-term rentals, now faces financial collapse as it evaluates restructuring options.

item.title: Five New Restaurants and One Reopening in San Diego
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: The Dish: Check out these five new restaurant openings and one reopening
Mi Pan Bakery opened its first brick-and-mortar location in Grantville, Mission Valley, after starting as a home-based business in 2020 by Alejandro Gomez and Alejandra Ruelas. The bakery offers French-inspired pastries and continues to operate at farmers markets. Rise Southern Biscuits expanded to El Cajon with a self-service model featuring online orders and pickup. Graze Craze launched a new charcuterie-themed location in Chula Vista, operated by Cameron and Veronica Davis. Philz Coffee opened its sixth San Diego County location in Mission Valley, offering fall drinks and pastries. Bacio di Latte expanded to Mission Valley, joining locations in Del Mar and La Jolla. Temaki Bar, an Encinitas restaurant, reopened after a six-week closure due to a basement fire, introducing a $10 Phoenix roll with proceeds benefiting the Encinitas Firefighter’s Association.

item.title: Songwriter Sanctuary Features Local Artists in San Diego Showcase
item.description:
Source: San Diego Reader stories Original headline: Live Five: Trevor Davis, Creepy Creeps, the Farmers, Shay Skylar, Songwriter Sanctuary
Trevor Davis, a San Diego musician, began his career in punk and gospel music, later performing on 'The Voice' and releasing albums. Songwriter Sanctuary's monthly event features local artists, including Ms. Connie, a bilingual singer-songwriter blending pop and Latin rhythms, and Sam Franz, who collaborated with American Idol alum Noel Tsoukalas. The Creepy Creeps, a surf punk band formed in 1999, known for their mariachi-costumed performances and 2013 San Diego Music Awards win. The Beat Farmers, an alternative rock band formed in 1983, continue with former members after key deaths. Shay Skylar, a North County artist influenced by Lifehouse and the Eagles, writes and produces his own music across genres. The event includes performances by The Sleepwalkers, nominated for San Diego Music Awards, and highlights local music scenes. Skylar notes his focus on rock, folk, and pop, citing influences from the 1960s to present.

item.title: Iowa Farmer Cuts Back Amid Soaring Fuel, Fertilizer, and Health Care Costs
item.description:
Source: Washington Post Original headline: How an Iowa farmer cut back as fuel, fertilizer and health care costs soared
Iowa farmer Aaron Lehman is cutting expenses as rising fuel, fertilizer, and health care costs strain his family farm. Lehman, 58, farms 500 acres in Iowa, relying on a 26-year-old combine he plans to replace later due to soaring costs. His family has faced declining profits since 2023, forcing him to reduce his farm salary by a third and halt retirement contributions. Fuel prices have risen 71% since last year, adding $1,000 daily to harvest costs, while fertilizer prices jumped 35% to $950 per ton. Health care costs tripled after ACA subsidies expired, prompting his wife to take a full-time physician assistant job to maintain coverage. The family also delayed buying a new car, cut streaming services, and limited travel to manage expenses. Lehman, president of the Iowa Farmers Union, endorsed Democrats in all five federal races for the first time, citing frustration with Trump’s trade policies and confusion over Iran tensions. He fears a repeat of the 1980s crisis, where young people abandoned farming, as his son balances farm work with an agronomist role. The Lehmans’ financial strain reflects broader rural concerns amid midterms.

item.title: Three Children in ICU After E. coli Linked to California Pumpkin Patch
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: 3 kids with E. coli are in ICU, as officials investigate California pumpkin patch
Three California children are in serious condition after contracting E. coli, prompting an investigation into Brookshire Farms. The San Luis Obispo County Department of Public Health reported five confirmed cases, potentially linked to the farm known for its pumpkin patches and corn mazes. Public Health Officer Tom Cuddy confirmed three of the cases were children receiving pediatric intensive care. The suspected exposure period at Brookshire Farms was Oct. 16-18, with the infection source still under investigation. Health officials urged anyone who visited the farm during those dates and experienced gastrointestinal symptoms to seek medical attention, noting children under 10 face higher complication risks. Brookshire Farms voluntarily closed and is cooperating with authorities. County Health Officer Dr. Christy Mulkerin emphasized efforts to identify the source and protect the community. E. coli infections can cause severe symptoms including kidney damage, and the farm posted on Facebook about its temporary closure. Co-owner Shawn Callaway expressed condolences to affected individuals.

item.title: Cheesecake Factory Reports Strong Earnings Amid Restaurant Industry Struggles
item.description:
Source: Washington Post Original headline: Joking aside, the Cheesecake Factory is seeing pretty good business
The Cheesecake Factory reported its second consecutive quarter of billion-dollar earnings, exceeding expectations. Its stock has more than doubled since January, reaching $110 per share. The company saw 15.2% year-over-year growth in comparable sales, outperforming a shrinking restaurant industry. Analysts attribute success to high-quality food, an extensive menu, and experiential value. The chain also benefits from a loyalty program and a viral TikTok trend featuring Cajun salmon. While the company hasn't commented on recent political remarks about its decor, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent dined at a location, noting the French dip cheeseburger. The Cheesecake Factory owns 15 other brands, though some show slower growth. Executives cited increased customer traffic and a 3% price hike as drivers, with average checks rising 3.1% despite the increase.

item.title: Spain's High-Speed Train Crash Kills at Least 68
item.description:
Source: BBC News, NPR Topics: News, Deutsche Welle, Washington Post - World Original headline: Spain's High-Speed Train Crash Kills at Least 68, Rescue Efforts Continue
Two high-speed trains collided near Toledo, Spain, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens. The crash occurred between Mora and Orgaz, 140 km south of Madrid, when a Renfe train struck an Iryo train stopped on the tracks. Rescue efforts continue as authorities search for survivors and bodies. Over 500 passengers were on board, with 64 confirmed dead and 58 injured. Former minister Fátima Báñez is among the missing. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared national mourning, suspending public events. Transport Minister Óscar Puente cited an 'inexplicable' decision by rail control to resume the Renfe train after a computer malfunction left a stop signal active. The train should not have been allowed to proceed without speed restrictions, he said. The crash marks Spain’s second deadly rail incident this year and the deadliest in Europe since 2013. Witnesses described the scene as 'apocalyptic.' Health Minister Mónica García confirmed emergency workers focus on rescuing survivors and recovering bodies. Civil Guard offices opened to assist families, with calls for blood donations. Sánchez vowed to investigate safety protocols. Spain’s royal family expressed 'shock and concern' via social media.
item.source: BBC News, NPR Topics: News, Deutsche Welle, Washington Post - World

item.title: AI Enables Sophisticated Fraud by Mimicking Authentic Documents
item.description:
Source: Harvard Business Review Original headline: Your Company’s Fraud Defenses Aren’t Ready for AI Threats
AI is enabling fraudsters to counterfeit voices, faces, and documents with ease, exploiting gaps between business functions even when individual systems remain secure. A 1963 case illustrates similar vulnerabilities. Tino De Angelis, a New Jersey commodities trader, defrauded lenders by forging warehouse receipts, claiming his company held vegetable oil in tanks. In reality, most tanks contained seawater with a thin oil film, and oil was moved between tanks to fool inspectors. When the scheme collapsed, $175 million in collateral was found to be non-existent. Lenders relied on the name printed on receipts, American Express Field Warehousing Corporation, as proof of verification, rather than actual assets. The case highlights how trust in institutional names persists, even when physical assets are fabricated. Modern AI threats mirror these historical vulnerabilities, as fraudsters can now replicate documents and identities with greater precision, challenging traditional fraud detection methods.

item.title: Mission Bay residents reinforce barriers against coastal flooding
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Mission Bay residents rush to prevent more flooding as high tides return
Mission Bay residents reinforced flood barriers Tuesday as high tides caused flooding. A coastal flood warning remains through Thursday, with water levels expected 1.7 feet above normal. Residents filled sandbags and city crews activated pumps to drain water. Philip Dupre reported Monday’s flooding reached his home’s first floor, prompting plans to block water with sandbags. He noted the 7.1-foot tide typically isn’t a major issue but warned a Kelvin wave could worsen flooding. Rebecca Ochoa shared flood videos, while Jacob Smith used water-filled tubes to reinforce barriers. The city rebuilt sand berms after they were damaged, though reports indicated people walked on them, rode wakeboards, and some unhoused individuals used them for shelter. Officials cautioned elevated water levels could continue posing a threat through Thursday.

item.title: Middle Eastern Powers Meet Iran to Avert Conflict
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Is Iran headed to war or peace after Mecca alliance meeting?
Middle Eastern powers Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey met Iran in Tehran to prevent military escalation. The trio, representing the Mecca defense pact, aimed to open negotiations and address regional tensions. Saudi Arabia emphasized avoiding renewed conflict, while Pakistan proposed a solution balancing US and Iranian interests. Iran hailed the talks as positive, with Supreme National Security Council head Mohsen Rezaei noting a new regional security atmosphere. Tehran also engaged with Russia and Qatar, framing the meetings as evidence of US diplomatic isolation. Analysts suggest the alliance serves deterrence rather than offensive goals, with Saudi Arabia seeking a diplomatic resolution to avoid economic risks. Pakistan's mediation role and Turkey's cautious approach were highlighted, while Iran emphasized continued diplomacy alongside military preparedness. No official breakthroughs were announced, but the talks underscored ongoing regional diplomacy amid tensions over Houthi attacks and the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Sicilian Dinner Recipes Offer Authentic Flavors Without Travel
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: This dinner can take you to Sicily, no passport needed
A Sicilian-inspired dinner features a fish pasta dish with a quick seafood ragù. The recipe uses roasted fish like sea bass, cod, or halibut, tossed with a sauce made from sweet peppers, white wine, and tomato. The pasta is served with olive oil and lemon, or with a simple sauce. Caponata, a savory-sweet condiment, is made with eggplant, zucchini, onions, and vinegar, simmered to meld flavors. A dessert of roasted pears, flavored with fennel seeds and topped with zabaglione, a custard made with Marsala wine, egg yolks, and sugar, completes the meal. The article details preparation steps for each dish, including substitution options for ingredients. Recipes emphasize fresh, seasonal produce and traditional Sicilian techniques like wood-fired roasting and hand-whisking zabaglione. Variations for caponata include artichokes or other vegetables, while the fish dish can use rockfish, sea bass, or corvina. The meal is presented as a way to experience Sicilian flavors without traveling.
